title: Two Points and a Ten: The Sixteenth Hands Mullin the Lot
title_candidates: Two Points and a Ten: The Sixteenth Hands Mullin the Lot
From Spoon to Both Prizes: Mullin's Kent Reversal
theme: Kent 2021 handed out its prizes in exactly the wrong order — the reigning Wooden Spoon holder took the Trophy AND the Jacket, the defending champion took the Spoon (while setting a course record), and the whole thing came down to one hole: the 16th, where Alex Baker made 10 twice and lost the Trophy by two.
tone: house — faithful, witty, tongue-in-cheek; Ronay/Peck register, gentle ribbing of insiders, every gag anchored to a number in the card
opening_hook: Open on the 16th tee at Prince's in R4 — Alex Baker fresh from 11 points in three holes, about to sign for a 10 on the second-easiest hole on the card — then loop back to Deal and explain how a two-point Trophy came to be decided there.
foreshadow: David Mullin arrives as reigning Wooden Spoon holder — 4 prior Spoons, Spoon in each of the last three TEGs — and promptly leads both boards from R1 H16
Jon Baker arrives as defending Trophy champion with back-to-back Jacket wins, and is last on the Trophy board by the 4th hole of R1
Alex Baker makes 10 at the 16th at Royal Cinque Ports in R1 — filed at the time as slapstick, not evidence
Mullin's cushion reads 8 points after R3 and only 2 at the end — the leader's grip loosened over the final round

competitions.name: Trophy (Stableford)
competitions.winner_or_loser: David Mullin (winner, 154 pts, by 2 from Alex Baker)
competitions.how: Mullin drew level at R1 H11 and went outright ahead at R1 H16 (b39) on the back of 13 points in four holes at Deal (b08) — and was never headed across the remaining 56 holes. A 41-point R2 at Littlestone stretched it to 9; a scrappier 36 at Prince's in R3, quadruple bogey at the 8th and all (b11), still left him 8 clear because nobody else could put a round together. R4 was the only day the Trophy was genuinely alive: Mullin's own quad at the 10th (b12) and Alex Baker's charge — 10 points in the first three holes (b13), 11 more from 13-15 (b10) — cut the margin to nothing much. Then Baker made 10 at the 16th, SI 17, the second-easiest hole on the card (b03, b29): 0 points where a par is worth 3. Mullin signed for 37 and 154 (b01); the reigning Spoon holder had won the Trophy for the third time in his career, by two.

competitions.name: Green Jacket (Gross)
competitions.winner_or_loser: David Mullin (winner, +68, by 7 from Jon Baker)
competitions.how: Alex Baker briefly drew level at R1 H6 (the last time anyone did); Mullin was level again by the 9th (b43-adjacent) and posted 87 at Royal Cinque Ports — a 7-shot personal best there — for a 5-shot cushion. R2 at Littlestone was the kill: 85 gross, another 7-shot course PB, and a Jacket lead of 12 that neither a +20 R3 nor a +19 R4 could put in danger. Final margin 7 (b02): Mullin's 9th Jacket, and his best Gross total's era-company noted by an all-time rank of 6. Behind him, Gregg Williams's +76 was a personal-best Gross total (b05) and still only good enough for the bronze medal in the Jacket race — the by-product of a field where everyone else improved too.

competitions.name: Wooden Spoon
competitions.how: The defending Trophy champion, three prior Trophies and three prior Jackets and no Spoons to his name, dropped to the bottom of the board at R1 H4 — a bogey at a par 3 of stroke index 18, the easiest hole at Deal (b35) — and stayed there for the remaining 68 holes of the tournament, bottom after every single round. The arithmetic was 29, 29, 28: seven shots worse than his last visit to Royal Cinque Ports, thirteen worse than his 79 at Littlestone in TEG 13, plus a quad at Prince's SI 1 13th in R3 (b18) and a triple at the 17th (b27). R4 was a different man entirely — 39 points, 14 of them in four holes from the 12th (b04, b41), and an 83 gross that is a new Prince's Shore/Dunes course record, beating 85 across five prior visits (cr01) — spoiled only by a quad at the last (b19). Too late by a distance: the Spoon was already engraved (b07).

rounds.chosen_headline: Deal, and the Reigning Spoon Holder Deals Himself In
rounds.angle: Mullin's 87 at Royal Cinque Ports — a 7-shot course PB — puts the man who has won the Spoon three TEGs running top of both boards by the 16th; Alex Baker posts his own course PB of 98 and still finds room for a 10; Jon Baker is last by the 4th and never gets up.

rounds.angle: Mullin's worst round of the tournament — a quadruple bogey 9 at the 8th, +20 for the day — costs him precisely one point of his cushion, because Williams's 39 (86 gross, a Prince's PB) is the only real answer and Jon Baker's 28, quad at SI 1, is the Spoon being welded shut.

headline_candidates: Ten at the Sixteenth, Two Points Short
Jon Baker Sets the Record, Keeps the Spoon
The Easiest Hole on the Card Decides a Trophy
rounds.chosen_headline: Ten at the Sixteenth, Two Points Short
rounds.angle: The counterfactual round: Alex Baker plays the best golf of his tournament — 10 points in three holes, 11 more from the 13th — and hands the Trophy back with a 10 at SI 17; Mullin survives his own quad at the 10th to win both prizes; Jon Baker breaks the Prince's course record with 83 and still collects the Spoon.

players.arc: Reigning Wooden Spoon holder with four Spoons and three in a row behind him, he opened with a 7-shot course PB at Deal, took the lead for good at R1 H16, added another 7-shot PB at Littlestone, personal bests at all three Kent courses, and turned up as champion of both the Trophy (154, third career win) and the Green Jacket (+68, ninth) — surviving a quad at the 8th in R3 and another at the 10th in R4 to hold on by two.

A one-time Trophy winner who spent four days alternating brilliance with arson — a course PB 98 at Deal containing a 10 at the 16th, 12 shots gone in four holes at Littlestone, quads at the 5th, 8th, 10th and 11th — and then, having got within touching distance with 21 points across two purple patches in R4, made 10 again at the 16th and lost the Trophy by two points.

Defending Trophy champion with back-to-back Jackets and no Spoons in his history, last on the board from the 4th hole of R1 and last after every round thereafter — before signing off with 39 points, 14 of them in four holes, and an 83 that is the new Prince's Shore/Dunes course record, which is the most gloriously Jon Baker way to collect a Wooden Spoon.

Three-time Trophy winner and perennial nearly-man who quietly posted the best Gross total of his TEG life at +76, including a Prince's personal best of 86 in R3 and a 12-point improvement on his R2 — and was still nowhere near either prize, which will surprise nobody less than him.

venue_notes: TEG's 2nd visit to Kent, England (Nov 2021) and a repeat of the TEG 13 itinerary, so every course-history comparison points back to last year: Royal Cinque Ports at Deal (2nd TEG round here — two Open Championships, brutal in wind) for R1; Littlestone's Championship Links on the Romney Marshes (2nd TEG round; Purves, refined by Braid and MacKenzie) for R2; Prince's Shore/Dunes at Sandwich for R3 and R4 (the 4th round being the 3rd TEG round at that venue). Four links days in November: use the wind and the marsh for atmosphere, and let Prince's — the venue of the 16th and of the course record — carry the closing act.
course_history_notes: David Mullin set new personal bests at all three Kent courses: 87 at Royal Cinque Ports in R1 (7 better than TEG 13), 85 at Littlestone in R2 (7 better), 91 at Prince's in R4 (1 better).

Jon Baker was 7 shots worse than his last visit to Royal Cinque Ports and 13 worse than his 79 at Littlestone in TEG 13 — then broke the Prince's course record with 83 in R4, 2 better than his own prior best there.
Alex Baker's new personal best at Royal Cinque Ports (98 in R1, 4 better than TEG 13) contained a 10 at the 16th; at Prince's he was 5 shots worse than last time.
Gregg Williams was 11 shots worse than his last visit to Littlestone but posted a Prince's personal best of 86 in R3 and a career-best Gross total of +76.
decisive_moments: Trophy: R4 H16 at Prince's — Alex Baker's 10 on the second-easiest hole on the card (SI 17) returned 0 points where a par is worth 3, leaving him two short of Mullin's 154 (b03, b01); the lead itself had been taken at R1 H16 (b39) and never surrendered.
Green Jacket: R2 at Littlestone — Mullin's 85 gross (a 7-shot course PB) opened a 12-shot Gross cushion that turned the last two rounds into a formality; final margin 7 (b02).

Wooden Spoon: R1 H4 at Royal Cinque Ports — Jon Baker's bogey at a par 3 of stroke index 18, the easiest hole at Deal, dropped him to the bottom of the Trophy board (b35), where he stayed for the remaining 68 holes (b07).

payoffs.payoff: He wins the Trophy on 154 (b01) AND the Green Jacket at +68 (b02) — the Spoon holder taking both prizes, with personal bests at all three Kent courses.

payoffs.seed: Alex Baker's 10 at the 16th at Royal Cinque Ports in R1 (b06), logged as slapstick
payoffs.payoff: He makes 10 at the 16th again in R4 (b03), this time on SI 17 with the Trophy live — 0 points where 3 would have won it, and he loses by two.

payoffs.seed: An 8-point cushion after R3 that finished at 2
payoffs.payoff: Mullin's quad at the 10th (b12) plus Alex Baker's 21 points across two R4 charges (b13, b10) ate the lead to almost nothing — the margin of victory was smaller than the leader's worst hole.

vehicle_fit_response.note: Taken up as supporting framing — a four-time Spoon winner and reigning Spoon holder winning both prizes is the best career line in years — but the close-finish rule is correct here: the 2-point margin and the 10 at the 16th make counterfactual the primary frame, with the twice-repeated 16th as motif.
